findings.file: tools/lints/_deps.py:PLAN_WRITERS (the _PW_EV rows, write_ci, _record_run) citing tests/test__evidence_io.py:6144 lk2
findings.issue: Read, not run: the seven helper-caller rows (_reconcile_subject, hold_full_run, keep_base, write_pointer, write_record, write_ci, _record_run) name `lk2` as the case showing each reads behind the lock. lk2 is an AST line-order check inside write_plan_file (read after acquire); it passes whatever a caller's `change(body)` returns, so a caller whose change closure returned a document read before the lock (the exact defect the two repairs had) would keep every one of these rows 'true'. The task asked for each row to carry the case that proves it, and the lint only checks that the case id exists in the suite.
findings.resolution: For the helper callers, cite a case per caller (or one parametrised interleaving case in the style of pa1-pa10) that lands a change between the caller's pre-lock work and its lock and asserts it survives; or word the row's reason as 'the helper reads behind the lock; the caller's change is derived from body (checked by <case>)' and add that case.

findings.issue: When every row found before the lock has moved by the time the plan is re-read, `rewrite` returns [] and apply_repair still saves the plan, journals a `scope.repair` row with empty `changes` and answers ok with 'journaled', i.e. reports a successful repair that rewrote nothing. repair-commits.py:_clear_under_lock handles the same situation with an explicit refusal ('changed in the plan since it was read ... re-run to look again'). The two repairs now disagree, and neither window-miss branch (`_still_lost` returning [], `applied == []`) has a case: rc12/rt16 only cover the record landing in the window, not the entry/commit moving.
findings.resolution: Refuse in apply_repair when `applied` is empty, with the same sentence as repair-commits, and add one case per repair that changes the entry/commit inside the window.

findings.issue: The task's tests.gate (tests__evidence_io, repair_commits, repair_tests_add, drive_phase, migrate_manifest, _deps) selects no case of merge-manifest.py, which the diff changed most (resolve's stray-target refusal, rw0-rw6); tests/test_merge_manifest.py and tests/test__deps.py's pw cases are also absent from tests.add. The recorded gate run therefore passed without exercising resolve at all; the executor's whole-tree sweep and red-first command did include it, but the declared gate does not.
findings.resolution: Add tests/test_merge_manifest.py (and test_close_phase/test_integrate_task if their files are in scope) to tests.gate and its rw cases to tests.add, so the recorded gate run covers the file the task changed.

findings.issue: The busy-lock reading is a substring match of INDEX_BUSY_HEAD over the runner's whole `out + err`, which also carries the gate's own failing lines; dl12 feeds a hand-built text, so nothing ties it to what run-test-gate.py:5681 really prints (`pointer:  NOT updated - <reason>`). A gate whose failing output quotes that sentence under an exit 3 would be read as a wait.
findings.resolution: Match on the pointer line (`NOT updated - ` + head) or have dl12 take its text from the runner's own renderer for a refused record; this keeps the rule bound to the runner's words.

findings.issue: The filed descriptive 'every plan writer ... now reads behind the index lock or refuses' overstates the layout converter: migrate-manifest.py:_changed_since narrows the window and its own docstring says a write landing between the re-read and the save is still lost; and the guide lists git's writes as outside the rule. The diff and guide are honest; the one-line claim is not.
findings.resolution: Say 'reads behind the lock, refuses on a change since its read, or is named as outside the rule'.

intent.note: Point 1: description 'ONE helper finds a repeat's source for every writer of a record' - diff adds repeat_source (_evidence_io.py) used by record_carrying, _put_record, reconcile and _reconciled; rv5 cases. Point 2: 'Fix both: re-read inside the locked section and recompute what is written from that read' - repair-commits _clear_under_lock re-reads and clears only where the fresh read still names the lost SHA; repair-tests-add apply_repair re-reads under the lock and applies rows by text; the class lint plan_writer_violations with PLAN_WRITERS/OTHER_WRITERS, a proving row, gate-parity rows and guide/CONTRIBUTING lines are present. Lows: relay_refusal reads run-test-gate exit 3 + INDEX_BUSY_HEAD as stop-index-lock; unwritable claim has its own sentence and still refuses (stated why in the guide); converter probe ml1 and a `_changed_since` refusal; git's unlocked writes named in the guide. Beyond the described list the diff also changes merge-manifest.py resolve (a refusal for strays); the plan's files list carries it. The executor's outcome describes the diff, except the descriptive overclaims for the converter (finding 5). Dependants answered in substance: repair commands' exit codes and refusal texts unchanged apart from the new re-read refusals; migrate command text unchanged (docstring now correctly cites layout.md).
